concepts.learning_objective: Explain what makes something in the environment a resource and why resources are a function of human activities.
Classify resources by origin, exhaustibility, ownership and status of development.

topics.title: Development of resources and sustainable development
topics.ncert_sections: Development of Resources; Sustainable Development; Rio Earth Summit; Agenda 21

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the problems caused by indiscriminate use of resources and the need for resource planning.
Explain the meaning of sustainable development and apply it to real situations.
Describe the Rio de Janeiro Earth Summit of 1992 and the objectives of Agenda 21.

topics.title: Resource planning and conservation
topics.ncert_sections: Resource Planning; Resource Planning in India; Conservation of Resources

concepts.learning_objective: State the steps involved in resource planning in India.
Analyse why availability of resources alone does not ensure development of a region.
Trace the ideas and milestones in resource conservation from Gandhiji to the Earth Summit.

topics.title: Land resources and land use pattern
topics.ncert_sections: Land Resources; Land Utilisation; Land Use Pattern in India

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the share of plains, mountains and plateaus in India's land area and their uses.
Distinguish between the categories of land use such as fallow land, culturable waste land, net sown area and gross cropped area.
Interpret the land use pattern of India and the physical and human factors behind it.
Identify the human activities that cause land degradation in different states of India.
Suggest suitable measures to check land degradation in arid, industrial and mining areas.

topics.title: Soil as a resource and classification of soils
topics.ncert_sections: Soil as a Resource; Classification of Soils

concepts.learning_objective: State the factors and processes responsible for the formation of soil.
Describe the distribution, properties and crops of alluvial and black soils.
Compare red and yellow, laterite, arid and forest soils in terms of formation and properties.
Explain the causes and types of soil erosion such as gully, sheet and wind erosion.
Choose suitable soil conservation methods such as contour ploughing, terracing, strip cropping and shelter belts.
